root_cause.text: During the transition to dynamic IDs in the SM8450 interconnect driver, the `.link_nodes` members of the `qhs_compute_cfg` and `qhs_lpass_cfg` node structures were left initialized with static integer IDs instead of pointers to the destination node structures, causing `icc_link_nodes()` to dereference an invalid pointer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that the `.link_nodes` initializers for `qhs_compute_cfg` and `qhs_lpass_cfg` in `drivers/interconnect/qcom/sm8450.c` were corrected from static IDs (`MASTER_CDSP_NOC_CFG` and `MASTER_CNOC_LPASS_AG_NOC`) to node pointers (`&qhm_nsp_noc_config` and `&qhm_config_noc`). Additionally, the commit message states that "The change to dynamic IDs for SM8450 platform interconnects left two links unconverted, fix it to avoid the NULL pointer dereference in runtime, when a pointer to a destination interconnect is not valid".

interconnect: qcom: sm8450: convert to dynamic IDs

Stop using fixed and IDs and covert the platform to use dynamic IDs
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 51513bec806fbe1cf9254baed97f115a480bbb53
Author: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@oss.qualcomm.com>
Date:   Fri Oct 31 16:45:37 2025 +0200

    interconnect: qcom: sm8450: convert to dynamic IDs
    
    Stop using fixed and IDs and covert the platform to use dynamic IDs for
    the interconnect. This gives more flexibility and also allows us to drop
    the .num_links member, saving from possible errors related to it being
    not set or set incorrectly.
    
    Signed-off-by: Dmitry
bic_trace_step.reason: In this commit, the node structures `qhs_compute_cfg` and `qhs_lpass_cfg` are incorrectly initialized with static integer IDs instead of pointers to the destination node structures. Specifically, `qhs_compute_cfg` has `.link_nodes = { MASTER_CDSP_NOC_CFG }` and `qhs_lpass_cfg` has `.link_nodes = { MASTER_CNOC_LPASS_AG_NOC }`. This causes `icc_link_nodes()` to dereference these integer values as pointers, leading to a crash.
